Adding context on the annotated dataflow:

- Step 1 (Ingress): Customer request lands at edge proxy in the requested region. We attach a region tag at the routing layer. No PII persisted here beyond transient request buffers.
- Step 2 (Preprocessing): Tokenization/redaction happens in a stateless preproc container. Tokenized identifiers are written to the inference prep KV with a short TTL (default 2 hours) — this is configurable per-customer.
- Step 3 (Inference): Model instances hold KV cache (session-level) in GPU memory; we do not persist per-session KV to disk by default. Prefix caching (shared prefix cache) is on dedicated caching nodes in the same region; TTLs and eviction policies are documented in the attached artifact.
- Step 4 (Logging & Audits): Audit logs for KMS usage and key access are streamed to our logging stack; we redact PII at the logging hook and only surface key IDs and operation metadata in plaintext.

I've placed an annotated PNG in Drive and included callouts for where TTL settings and access controls sit. Note two important operational controls: customer-configured data residency flag (forces region-level routing) and an emergency cross-region access workflow that requires two approvers and is logged to a separate immutable ledger.

Attachments referenced: annotated-dataflow-acme.png (Drive link in my note).

Mina

Quick technical clarifications — pulling these into the packet:

- Geofencing/routing: We implement a two-layer routing policy: L1 (ingress region affinity) and L2 (model placement affinity). L1 is enforced by edge proxies (envoy policies) and validated in CI with synthetic requests that assert the egress region. I'll attach the test harness snippet.
- Cross-border subprocessors: Infra (cloud compute) is a cross-border subprocessor only in the sense that managed backups (long-term archives) may be replicated for DR; for Acme we can opt-out of cross-region replication and keep backups in-region. That decision needs contractual binding in the DPA annex — I'll note it as an optional clause.
- KMS custody: Keys are customer-shared (BYKMS) for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys and per-customer key separation. Audit sample: see kms-ownership-attestation.pdf (contains redacted key usage with timestamps).

Attachment stubs I'll include in the packet: routing-test-harness.zip (script + results), kms-ownership-attestation.pdf (redacted), annotated-dataflow-acme.png.

Marcus
Director, Serving Infrastructure
